title: Exposed API
summary: An API debug endpoint is leaking sensitive configuration in production.
briefing:
NebulaCorp's web application firewall flagged an anomaly: the /api/debug/config endpoint should return 403 to all callers, but the access log shows at least one successful 200 response.

You have two files:
- access.log — the HTTP access log from the production reverse proxy
- debug-response.json — the response body captured by the WAF for the anomalous 200 request

Examine both files. The response body contains leaked secrets, including a flag. Find it and submit it.
objectives: Find the 200-status request to /api/debug/config in the access log
Note the source IP and user agent of the successful request
Read the captured response body for leaked secrets
Submit the flag from the response

hints.title: Narrow the search
hints.text: grep "debug/config" access.log shows all requests to that endpoint. Compare the status codes.

hints.title: Response file
hints.text: The flag is a JSON field in debug-response.json. Use jq or just read the file.

artifacts.description: HTTP access log from the production reverse proxy (~300 entries).
Captured response body from the anomalous request.
